sections.title: Many-flowered rose
sections.text: A fast-growing scrambling shrub or liana native from the eastern Himalaya through China, Korea and Japan. Arching, prickly stems can form dense thickets; plants commonly reach about 1.8–3 m, sometimes more. White to pale-pink flowers, usually 2.5–5 cm across, occur in large clusters, followed by small red hips under 1 cm across.

sections.title: Fruit and comparison
sections.text: The hips are eaten by wildlife and are reported as edible for people; remove the seed hairs before eating. In North America the species is an invasive shrub. Its many small white flowers distinguish it from the larger, pink flowers of several native eastern North American roses.
